A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LaMP-QA research work. All 21 pages of each version, including Appendices A–G, are readable, and the text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original baseline experiments in Tables 2–3, human annotation results, and analyses of retrieval context and automatic evaluators.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports human preference percentages and an oracle-plan experiment in Figures 1 and 3.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same retrieval, learned aspect planning, response generation, and cross-entropy training procedures. The new gold-plan condition is an experimental control; it does not revise the proposed PlanPers method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SE-PQA-derived LaMP-QA data across Arts & Entertainment, Lifestyle & Personal Development, and Society & Culture. Table 1 and the subcategory distributions are unchanged; the added analyses use existing task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 3 adds a gold-plan oracle variant as a comparator to PlanPers with its trained planner. Tables 2–3 retain the same non-personalized, random-profile RAG, asker-profile RAG, and PlanPers comparisons and generator backbones.

E3.justification: The added oracle experiment supplies rubric-derived gold plans during generation with Qwen 2.5 Instruct 7B. Existing splits, metrics, training budgets, and retrieval settings remain unchanged. V1 already describes a 100-example, two-rater human comparison of the same systems; v2 does not establish an additional annotation run.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds a focused planning-headroom analysis comparing learned plans with gold rubric aspects in Figure 3. The existing random-profile controls, retrieved-item sensitivity, evaluator-size analysis, and position-bias analysis, including appendix results, are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain the t-test reporting at p < 0.05 and Cohen's kappa values of 0.87 and 0.726 for the existing annotation studies. The newly reported preference percentages and oracle scores introduce no confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run information.

E6.justification: Figure 1 adds human preferences of 35% for PlanPers, 26% for RAG-Personalization, and 39% ties. Figure 3 adds gold-plan scores of 0.7320, 0.7933, and 0.8140, with macro-average 0.7797, alongside retained trained-planner scores of 0.3518, 0.4818, and 0.5240, averaging 0.4525. Tables 2–3 and all original plots retain their results.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, mathematical definitions, and evaluation Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The new oracle 'upper bound' discussion describes an empirical comparison, without introducing a formal bound or proof.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution, aspect-based evaluation, planning approach, and headline improvement of up to 39% retain their meaning and scope. The conclusion's more explicit emphasis on planning restates findings already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the human preference breakdown as support for better alignment with user needs and the oracle gap as substantial headroom for improving planning. These interpretations extend the discussion; the four existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The added human-comparison paragraph explicitly describes random sampling and says annotators received personalized rubrics alongside questions and narratives. These are additional documented details, without establishing that the earlier study was rerun. Appendix E's implementation settings, appendix prompts, and code/data destinations are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to LaMP, LongLaMP, personalized retrieval, and earlier personalization methods. No substantive research-positioning change is evident.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited wording edits in the front matter, introduction, conclusion, and AI-assistance disclosure, adds two experimental discussion paragraphs, and moves acknowledgments before Limitations. The overall section and appendix structure is preserved.

P2.justification: V2 adds a human-preference pie chart and an oracle-comparison bar chart as Figures 1 and 3. Existing figures and tables are retained with renumbering and page reflow, including the validation plot moving from Figure 14 to Figure 16.

improvement.justification: The human win/tie breakdown and oracle comparison modestly strengthen the evidence and clarify planning headroom while preserving existing results and reproducibility information. These benefits are tempered by a numerical reporting error: Figure 3 implies approximately 55–108% relative gains, whereas the text claims 155–208%. The correct plotted scores still support substantial headroom, but the percentage overstatement and lack of uncertainty for the added comparisons limit the improvement.
